title: Lesson 9
paragraph: 費用・成果・お金の判断

words.meaning: to have income equal to costs, with no profit or loss
words.japaneseMeaning: 収支がとんとんになる
words.example: The café needs more customers just to break even.

sentencePractice.prompt: The café earns exactly enough to cover every cost, with no profit and no loss. At this level of sales, it can only ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Income exactly equals costs. A profit requires income above costs; a loss requires costs above income.

words.meaning: to have enough money to pay for basic living costs
words.japaneseMeaning: 必要な生活費を何とか賄う
words.example: With higher rent, it is harder for the family to make ends meet.

words.word: cost an arm and a leg
words.meaning: to cost a very large amount of money
words.example: Repairs to that old car can cost an arm and a leg.

words.meaning: to produce a good result after effort or time
words.example: All those hours of practice finally paid off at the concert.
words.usageNote: ここでは努力がよい結果につながる意味。借金を完済する pay off a debt とは区別します。

words.meaning: to skip proper steps in order to save time, effort, or money
words.japaneseMeaning: 手間や費用を惜しんで必要な工程を省く
words.example: We cannot cut corners when checking the safety of the equipment.

words.meaning: something that is unfairly expensive for what you receive
words.japaneseMeaning: 値段に見合わない品やサービス、ぼったくり
words.example: Ten pounds for a tiny bottle of water felt like a rip-off.
words.usageNote: くだけた表現。ここでは価格が不当に高いという意味で、模倣品を指す用法とは区別します。

words.meaning: to receive enough value or enjoyment for the amount you paid
words.japaneseMeaning: 払った金額に見合う価値を得る
words.example: Use the museum pass several times to get your money's worth.

words.meaning: to spend more money than you can afford
words.japaneseMeaning: 収入や資力を超えた生活をする
words.example: Borrowing for everyday luxuries can lead you to live beyond your means.

words.meaning: with only a small amount of money available to spend
words.example: We planned the wedding on a tight budget.

words.meaning: to pay the whole cost of something
words.example: The company agreed to foot the bill for the repairs.

sentencePractice.prompt: The company will pay the entire repair cost; no employee will contribute. The company will ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Paying everything is footing the bill. Sharing divides the cost; passing it on transfers payment to another person.
